chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: The Depression at school
summary: The Depression barely touched him; the president gave him a gold trumpet.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Now, we talked a little bit before in that, sort of a chronological order. And, one of the things we didn't focus on too much, I think was because you were jumping right from your childhood right into 'Bama State and things of that sort. Did you have any comments on the Depression? You know, the overall environment, the artistic environment, or whatever, during the Depression? You didn't focus on that too much.
Well, I didn't know, it didn't bother me too much because I was in both schools. You know?

I didn't have to worry too much about that cause I was in school and whatever I needed, I got it there. The President of 'Bama State, he liked me very much. If I wanted to go to a show, I'd go up and tell him. I'd say Pres, I want to go to a movie. Now, he knew what I'd come there for. He used to go in his pocket and give me $2.00 so I could have my chance to go to the show and come back. You know? So, that's all I needed. You know, I was there on the campus. Cause in both schools, high school and 'Bama State College, I was on the campus. And so, I'd go out and I'd visit. And the teachers, all the teachers were very nice to me. Sometimes they'd have me out to dinner. In Birmingham, when I was on the basketball team, they used to call me Boss
Hawkins. How old was I? I must have been about 12, 14 years old. I was the captain of the team. You know? So, I used to get along with the students and the teachers, the faculty, and the president.

When I left there, the president knew I wasn't coming back. He gave me a gold trumpet. He gave me my first trumpet. I was playing cornet. I had the cornet I was playing through school. He gave me my first trumpet to show his, you know, appreciating me being there.
